correctness.rationale: The polyhedral-cone volume 2πR²h/3 and lateral area 2πR√(R²+h²) combine with the directional width 2max(R√(1−u²),h u). Integrating u∈[0,1] gives mean width R[x+arctan(1/x)], so the normalized Steiner cubic is 2z³/3+a z²+b z+x/3 with b=√(1+x²). The strict Minkowski inequality for a non-ball implies a²>2b; stationary z±=(-a±q)/2 are negative. Their exact critical values are Φ∓/6, with q=√(a²−2b). Independent symbolic expansion verifies Φ± prime =1/2+3/2[(x/b)(a±q)−1]²>0 for all x>0. The limits at x↓0 are both negative; derivative >1/2 forces a unique zero of each; Φ+>Φ− orders them. The packaged rational sign brackets (1/2,3/5) and (23/20,6/5) isolate the zeros. The standard cubic sign diagram proves multiplicities and all root cases; no finite sampling substitutes for global monotonicity.

value.rationale: A symmetric double cone is a canonical one-parameter singular convex-body family. Determining whether all three Steiner roots are real is sensitive to intrinsic volume structure; the exact reentrant complex–real–complex transition with two rigorously unique boundary aspects is not just a plotted sample or generic cubic formula. Its strict-square monotonicity mechanism may serve as a worked structural benchmark for Steiner-root geometry.
residual_risks: No classification of tilted, elliptical or asymmetric double cones.

limitations: x=h/R>0 only; thresholds are unique analytic zeros, not elementary closed forms.
